questions.q: What is a computer network?
o: A set of computers connected together to share resources
A single computer with many files
questions.e: A network is a set of connected computers sharing resources.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a computer network?
questions.e: Networks exist so computers can share resources.

questions.q: Which of the following is a resource commonly shared over a network?
questions.e: Files, printers, and services are shared resources.

questions.q: What is an end device?
o: A computing device that interconnects and has a unique IP address
questions.e: End devices are computing devices, each with a unique IP address.

questions.q: Which is an example of an end device?
questions.e: A laptop is a computing end device with an IP address.

questions.q: What do intermediary devices do?
o: Provide connectivity, connect networks, and connect segments within a network
questions.e: Intermediary devices move data between devices and networks.

questions.q: Which category is NOT listed under intermediary devices?
questions.e: The listed types are access, internetworking, communication servers/modems, and security devices.

questions.q: What is an Ethernet hub used for?
o: Connecting multiple computers so they act as a single segment
questions.e: A hub connects computers into one segment.

questions.q: What does a switch do?
o: Connects devices together on a computer network
questions.e: A switch connects devices within a network.

questions.q: What is the role of a router?
o: Joining multiple computer networks via wired or wireless connections
questions.e: Routers join multiple networks together.

questions.q: A Network Interface Card is also known as what?
questions.e: NIC stands for Network Interface Card.

questions.q: What does a network card do?
o: Connects a computer with the network
questions.e: A NIC is the hardware that connects a computer to the network.

questions.q: What is the function of a modem?
o: Enables a computer to transmit data over a connection and brings internet service from an ISP
Connects multiple networks as a router
questions.e: Modems transmit data and deliver ISP internet service.

questions.q: Which device typically brings internet service from an Internet Service Provider?
questions.e: The modem connects the home or office to the ISP.

questions.q: A device joins a home network to the ISP and also routes traffic to several devices. Which combination is described?
questions.e: The modem brings the ISP link and the router distributes traffic.

questions.q: Which application uses a network to allow multiplayer games between devices?
questions.e: Networked games allow multiplayer play across devices.

questions.q: How do networks support database applications?
o: Each computer must copy the database offline
Databases only work on one PC
Different computers can access the same database
questions.e: Networks let multiple computers access a shared database.

questions.q: Which is a network application for sending and receiving messages?
questions.e: Email sends and receives messages over networks.

questions.q: Which applications are examples of video conferencing?
questions.e: These apps enable video conferencing over networks.

questions.q: What does FTP stand for?
questions.e: FTP is the File Transfer Protocol.

questions.q: What is FTP mainly used for?
o: Exchanging files over the web using a network connection
questions.e: FTP exchanges files across a network.

questions.q: What does LAN stand for?
questions.e: LAN is a Local Area Network.

questions.q: Which best describes a LAN?
o: A network of only two countries
A network that usually spans a single geographical area
questions.e: LANs cover a single geographical area and serve one organization.

questions.q: What does MAN stand for?
questions.e: MAN is a Metropolitan Area Network.

questions.q: A MAN usually interconnects LANs using what?
questions.e: MANs use a high-capacity backbone and provide uplinks to WANs.

questions.q: What geographic coverage can a MAN provide?
questions.e: MAN coverage can span between cities.

questions.q: What does WAN stand for?
questions.e: WAN is a Wide Area Network.

questions.q: Which best describes a WAN?
o: A network inside one building only
A network connection between two or more LANs over a large geographic distance
questions.e: WANs connect LANs across large distances.

questions.q: What device handles communication between a LAN and other networks in a WAN setup?
questions.e: A gateway handles communication between LANs and other networks.

questions.q: What is the client-server model?
o: A relationship where clients request services and servers provide them
A model where all computers are servers
questions.e: Clients request information; servers provide it.

questions.q: What do servers do in the client-server model?
o: Provide information and services to clients
questions.e: Servers host information and services for clients.

questions.q: What do clients do in the client-server model?
o: Request and display information obtained from the server
questions.e: Clients request data and present it to the user.

questions.q: What is network topology?
o: The arrangement of computers in a network
questions.e: Topology is how computers are arranged and connected.

questions.q: Which topology connects every computer and device to a single cable?
questions.e: Bus topology uses one shared cable.

questions.q: Which topology forms a ring with the last computer connected to the first?
questions.e: Ring topology forms a closed loop.

questions.q: Which topology connects all computers to a single hub through a cable?
questions.e: Star topology uses a central hub.

questions.q: In which topology do all nodes cooperate to distribute data among each other?
questions.e: Mesh nodes cooperate and distribute data.

questions.q: Which topology combines two or more standard topologies?
questions.e: Hybrid topology combines multiple topologies.

questions.q: Which topology is most vulnerable to a single cable failure affecting the whole network?
questions.e: A bus has one shared cable, so a break can disrupt the segment.

questions.q: Which topology offers redundant paths between nodes?
questions.e: Mesh provides multiple paths, improving redundancy.

questions.q: A school lab connects every PC to one central switch. This is which topology?
questions.e: A central device with individual links is a star.

questions.q: Which topology is arranged as a closed loop?
questions.e: Ring topology loops back to the first node.

questions.q: What is a network protocol?
questions.e: Protocols are rules for communication.

questions.q: A group of related protocols needed to communicate electronically is called what?
questions.e: Related protocols together form a protocol suite.

questions.q: Which is NOT something networking protocols describe?
o: How errors are passed between devices
The format or structure of a message
questions.e: Protocols describe message format, sharing, errors, and sessions, not cable color.

questions.q: What does HTTP stand for?
questions.e: HTTP is the Hypertext Transfer Protocol.

questions.q: What does HTTP govern?
o: Interaction between a web server and a web client
questions.e: HTTP governs web server and client interaction.

questions.q: What does TCP stand for?
questions.e: TCP is the Transmission Control Protocol.

questions.q: What does TCP handle?
o: Individual conversations between servers and clients
questions.e: TCP manages conversations between servers and clients.

questions.q: HTTP messages are divided by TCP into smaller pieces called what?
questions.e: TCP segregates messages into segments.

questions.q: What does IP stand for?
questions.e: IP is the Internet Protocol.

questions.q: What is IP used for by routers?
o: Selecting the best path to the destination host
questions.e: Routers use IP to choose the best path.

questions.q: A message received by a host usually contains what?
o: Only one protocol with no data
Multiple protocols plus the actual data
questions.e: Messages carry multiple protocols and the data.

questions.q: Which protocol is given as an example of an application header?
questions.e: The application header may be HTTP.

questions.q: Which device joins multiple computer networks together?
questions.e: Routers join multiple networks.

questions.q: Which device connects computers into a single shared segment?
questions.e: A hub creates one segment.

questions.q: Which device is the hardware interface between a computer and a network?
questions.e: The NIC connects the computer to the network.

questions.q: Which device converts signals so a computer can transmit data over a line to an ISP?
questions.e: Modems transmit data over the ISP connection.

questions.q: Which network type connects offices in two different continents?
questions.e: WANs span large geographic distances.

questions.q: Which network type interconnects LANs across a city using a backbone?
questions.e: MANs cover metropolitan areas and interconnect LANs.

questions.q: What is a set of computers connected together to share resources called?
questions.e: A network connects computers to share resources.

questions.q: What type of device has a unique IP address and interconnects in a network?
questions.e: End devices are computing hosts with unique IPs.

questions.q: What type of device provides connectivity and connects networks and segments?
questions.e: Intermediary devices connect devices, networks, and segments.

questions.q: What device connects multiple computers so they act as a single segment?
questions.e: A hub connects computers into one segment.

questions.q: What device connects devices together on a computer network and forwards data intelligently?
questions.e: Switches connect devices within a network.

questions.q: What small electronic device joins multiple computer networks via wired or wireless connections?
questions.e: Routers join multiple networks.

questions.q: What does NIC stand for?
questions.e: NIC means Network Interface Card.

questions.q: What device enables a computer to transmit data over a line and brings internet service from an ISP?
questions.e: A modem transmits data and connects to the ISP.

questions.q: What network type spans a single geographical area and serves one organization?
questions.e: LAN covers a single geographic area.

questions.q: What network type interconnects LANs across a city using a backbone?
questions.e: MAN interconnects LANs across a city.

questions.q: What network type connects two or more LANs over a large geographic distance?
questions.e: WAN connects LANs over long distances.

questions.q: What device in a WAN handles communication between a LAN and other networks?
questions.e: A gateway bridges the LAN and other networks.

questions.q: What model describes clients requesting services and servers providing them?
questions.e: The client-server model separates requesters and providers.

questions.q: What is the arrangement of computers in a network called?
questions.e: Topology is the network's arrangement.

questions.q: Which topology connects every device to a single shared cable?
questions.e: Bus topology uses one cable.

questions.q: Which topology connects computers in a closed loop?
questions.e: Ring topology loops end to end.

questions.q: Which topology connects all computers to a single central hub?
questions.e: Star topology uses a central hub.

questions.q: Which topology has all nodes cooperate to distribute data among each other?
questions.e: Mesh nodes distribute data cooperatively.

questions.q: Which topology combines two or more standard topologies?
questions.e: Hybrid combines multiple topologies.

questions.q: What do we call the rules that govern communications?
questions.e: Protocols are communication rules.

questions.q: Which protocol governs interaction between a web server and a web client?
questions.e: HTTP governs web client and server interaction.

questions.q: Which protocol handles individual conversations and splits messages into segments?
questions.e: TCP manages conversations and segmentation.

questions.q: Which protocol is used by routers to select the best path to the destination host?
questions.e: IP supports path selection by routers.

questions.q: What are the smaller pieces called that TCP creates from HTTP messages?
questions.e: TCP divides messages into segments.

questions.q: What application protocol is used for exchanging files over the web?
questions.e: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol.

questions.q: A computer network is a set of computers connected to share resources.
questions.e: That is the lesson definition.

questions.q: Every end device has a unique IP address.
questions.e: End devices are identified by unique IP addresses.

questions.q: Routers are used [[only to connect one computer to a single network]].
questions.e: Routers join multiple networks.

questions.q: An Ethernet hub connects multiple computers so they act as a single segment.
questions.e: That is a hub's role.

questions.q: A switch and a NIC are the [[same]] device.
questions.e: A switch is not a NIC.

questions.q: A LAN usually spans a single geographical area.
questions.e: LANs cover one geographic area.

questions.q: A MAN typically spans [[multiple continents]].
questions.e: MANs cover metropolitan areas and between cities.

questions.q: A WAN connects two or more LANs over a potentially large geographic distance.
questions.e: That is the WAN definition.

questions.q: In the client-server model, [[clients provide services and servers request them]].
questions.fix: servers provide services and clients request them
questions.e: The roles are reversed in the statement.

questions.q: [[Bus topology]] connects all computers to a central hub.
questions.e: A central hub describes star topology; bus uses one cable.

questions.q: In ring topology, the last computer is connected back to the first.
questions.e: Ring topology forms a loop.

questions.q: In mesh topology, all nodes cooperate to distribute data among each other.
questions.e: Mesh enables cooperative data distribution.

questions.q: Hybrid topology combines two or more topologies.
questions.e: Hybrid mixes standard topologies.

questions.q: HTTP governs interaction between a web server and a web client.
questions.e: HTTP is the web's application protocol.

questions.q: [[TCP]] is the protocol routers use to select the best path to a destination.
questions.e: IP is used for path selection by routers.
